analysis: Integration of all 15 units. The substantive change is in SSDWriteBehind.swift: for jobs with more than one block, the new chargeWholeDonation (head lines ~339-352) sums SSDBlockStore.serializedByteCount over all blocks with overflow checks and makes one rateLimiter.tryConsume. The prepaid flag (head line ~276) skips per-block tryConsume (head lines ~302-309). If the sum fails, overflows or is refused, nothing is charged and the original per-block charge path runs, so the daily endurance cap (T-041 guard) is not weakened. Total charged bytes equal the per-block sum. Blocks skipped after prepay stay charged, which is conservative. Charges still precede writes and are never refunded. The low-disk floor and ENOSPC cooldown checks run before the charge, and the index-last ordering and settlement callbacks are unchanged. Other changes are docs (ssd-kv-cache.md 390-400), a changelog, a comment in SSDPrefixCache.swift (1081-1083) and a test comment, plus a new ledger-charge test file. None of them touch DBK3 crypto, HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping, TTL, KEK handling or path-safety controls. Minor observation: with a prepaid charge, the outcome for partial failures reports writeFailed rather than writeRateLimited, and prepaid charges for dropped blocks over-count. Both are availability or telemetry effects, not security regressions. Unverified: the SSDWriteRateLimiter.tryConsume implementation (cross-process ledger, flock, fail-closed behavior) is outside the supplied evidence, and the replayed source is incomplete (32 units omitted). The new test file was only reviewed through other passes' summaries. Nothing indicates a bypass, so I record this as a coverage limit rather than a finding.
